question: How does nitrogen limitation affect PHB accumulation in Cupriavidus necator?

claims.text: Cupriavidus necator is described as a non-growth-associated PHB producer, so nitrogen limitation is the commonly used lever to halt biomass growth and drive intracellular PHB accumulation.

passages.quote: C. necator is a typical type of non-growth associated PHB-producing bacteria.

claims.text: In the C. necator fermentation review, nitrogen limitation is the more commonly used nutrient-limiting approach for PHB production, with phosphate limitation having a similar stimulating effect.

passages.quote: Among the nutrient limiting conditions, nitrogen limitation is the more commonly used approach.
In addition to nitrogen limitation, phosphate limiting conditions have a similar effect to stimulate intracellular PHB accumulation.

claims.text: Complete removal of nitrogen supply in C. necator cultures, with pH controlled by a sodium base instead of an ammonium base, can give high PHB accumulation but also low biomass, which can leave the overall PHB content low.

passages.quote: Moreover, many studies have also found that although a high C/N ratio or a completely 0% nitrogen supply led to high PHB accumulation in C. necator, this extreme condition can also lead to low biomass production which resulted in an overall low PHB content.

claims.text: In a bakery-waste hydrolysate fermentation, PHB content as a percentage of cell dry weight rose and the authors attributed the rise to nitrogen limitation; this record's provenance is unverified and its strain and conditions are not stated.

In a Burkholderia sacchari xylose study, PHA content as a percentage of cell dry weight under nitrogen limitation is recorded, but this is a different organism from C. necator and the record is unverified.

Nitrogen deficiency did not improve PHB accumulation in engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae; the highest PHB contents came under nitrogen-replete conditions, so the nitrogen-limitation response seen in natural bacterial producers does not carry over to that yeast.

passages.quote: In contrast to what was observed in natural PHB-producing bacteria, nitrogen deficiency did not improve PHB accumulation in S. cerevisiae.

gaps: No controlled C. necator study in the corpus directly compares PHB content (% CDW) and biomass at nitrogen-limited versus nitrogen-replete conditions with stated strain and carbon source; the C. necator PHB values found are unverified records whose conditions are not stated.

The only quantitative nitrogen-limitation records for C. necator-related work are curation notes from unverified extractions (bakery waste, mixed review tables); their nitrogen levels, C:N ratios, and timing of limitation are not given.
The corpus lacks time-course data (biomass, PHB, residual ammonium, carbon uptake) showing when nitrogen runs out and how the carbon split between growth and storage changes.
No evidence on the optimal nitrogen depletion point or the trade-off between PHB content and total PHB titer in C. necator beyond one review's qualitative remark.

passages.heading: Current Strategies Used to Enhance PHB Production Efficiencies › Fermentation Strategies › Nutrient Limitation
passages.text: C. necator is a typical type of non-growth associated PHB-producing bacteria. Therefore, non-carbon nutrients’ limitation has been a widely used approach for C. necator to inhibit biomass production and enable intracellular PHB accumulation. In most of the studies, the nutrient limiting conditions, which generally refer to depletion of nitrogen and phosphorus, are complemented to improve the PHB production yield using C. necator. Among the nutrient limiting conditions, nitrogen limitation is the more commonly used approach. In some of the studies, researchers completely removed the nitrogen source to improve PHB accumulation. Under these extreme cases, pH control is monitored through NaOH instead of NH4OH to achieve a 0% nitrogen supply.

passages.heading: Current Strategies Used to Enhance PHB Production Efficiencies › Fermentation Strategies › Nutrient Limitation
passages.text: Under these extreme cases, pH control is monitored through NaOH instead of NH4OH to achieve a 0% nitrogen supply. However, it was also proved by several studies that PHB production in C. necator could be negatively affected due to the accumulation of Na+ ions when NaOH is used. In addition to nitrogen limitation, phosphate limiting conditions have a similar effect to stimulate intracellular PHB accumulation. The trigger mechanism of phosphate limiting conditions can be related to the fact that phosphorus feeding influences the NADPH availability and resultant PHB accumulation kinetics. Moreover, many studies have also found that although a high C/N ratio or a completely 0% nitrogen supply led to high PHB accumulation in C. necator, this extreme condition can also lead to low biomass production which resulted in an overall low PHB content.

passages.heading: Abstract
passages.text: TMB4443 accumulated most PHB under aerobic conditions and with glucose as sole carbon source, whereas the highest PHB concentrations were obtained with TMB4425 under anaerobic conditions and xylose as carbon source. In both cases, the highest PHB contents were obtained with high availability of nitrogen. The major impact of nitrogen availability was observed in TMB4425, where a 2.7-fold increase in PHB content was obtained. In contrast to what was observed in natural PHB-producing bacteria, nitrogen deficiency did not improve PHB accumulation in S. cerevisiae. Instead the excess available carbon from xylose was shunted into glycogen, indicating a significant gluconeogenic activity on xylose.
